evals.name: schema-design
evals.prompt: Design the database schema for adding multi-tenant workspaces to our app — orgs, members, roles, and per-org billing. We're on Postgres. I want this solid before we build.
evals.expected_output: Routes schema_design to top/xhigh, queues second_opinion extra (top, background), one-line routing justification in window-burn framing, no model question asked.
assertions: schema_design resolves to tier=top effort=xhigh (visible in script_calls resolve_model output)
second_opinion extra appears in the extras/dispatch plan as a background run
routing justification line present in window-burn framing; user is never asked which model to use

evals.name: lint-sweep
evals.prompt: ruff just flagged about 40 lint errors across src/ (unused imports, f-strings, line length). Clean them all up.
evals.expected_output: Routes to light/low (mechanical volume lane); explicitly avoids top-tier waste; may parallelize within fanout cap.
assertions: main lint work routed to light tier at low effort
no top or frontier tier appears in the dispatch plan for the lint work (no top-tier waste)
background extras stay within fanout_cap (3); the fresh cap of 5 is NOT self-declared (only 'throttle fresh' or a host window signal justifies it)

evals.name: unit-tests

assertions: unit_tests resolves to tier=mid effort=high
test_gap extra queued at mid tier OR explicitly skipped in one line as redundant with a test-writing main lane
background extras stay within fanout_cap (3); the fresh cap of 5 is NOT self-declared (only 'throttle fresh' or a host window signal justifies it)

evals.name: security-review

assertions: security_review resolves to top tier, NOT frontier, with the adapter pin acknowledged
the frontier model appears nowhere in the security work's dispatch plan
security_sweep is either queued OR explicitly skipped in one line as redundant with the security_review main lane

background extras include diff_review and docs_sync (edge_case_hunt acceptable too), all background

lint_sweep-class extras resolve via --task boilerplate_scaffolding with no fallback_route bounce

evals.name: state-gate-sequence
evals.prompt: Simulate this exact sequence of user turns, handling each per the skill, showing each turn's user-visible response: (a) bare '/mouter'; (b) 'refactor the error handling in src/app.py'; (c) '/mouter fix this race condition in src/utils.py'; (d) '/mouter status'; (e) bare '/mouter'; (f) 'add input validation to the report command'.
evals.expected_output: (a) toggles OFF with one-line confirm; (b) SILENT stand-down — no routing, no mention of mouter; (c) one-shot full pipeline, state stays OFF; (d) status card showing OFF; (e) toggles ON; (f) auto-routes with no model question.
assertions: turn (a) toggles OFF with a one-line confirmation
turn (b) is a SILENT stand-down: no mention of mouter, routing, tiers, or models
turn (c) runs the full pipeline as a one-shot AND state remains OFF afterward
turn (d) status shows OFF plus a status card
turn (e) toggles back ON
turn (f) auto-routes with no model question asked

evals.name: throttle-low
evals.prompt: First handle the mouter command 'throttle low'. Then the user asks: 'implement the CSV export feature for the report module with tests'. Show the routing and extras behavior.
evals.expected_output: throttle persisted to low; extras shed per degradation_order (reduce, downband, defer) BEFORE main-lane quality; downgrades announced; main lane stays band-matched.
assertions: throttle override persisted to low via mouter_state.py (visible in script_calls)
extras shed per degradation_order (reduced/downbanded/deferred) and the downgrade announced
main-lane routing stays band-matched (not degraded below its band)
